eligibility.evidence: Sec 3.2, 4: GPT-2 completions (1000 sampled per sub-phrase) feed a new 'incompatibility fraction' measure, tested on the Pickering & Traxler (1998) garden-path items and compared with human reading times and surprisal (Tables 1-4). Borderline because GPT-2 is a component of a modelling framework rather than a participant, and its size is not stated.

A.title: How can large language models become more human?
A.venue: Workshop on Cognitive Modeling and Computational Linguistics (CMCL 2024)

paradigms.name: Garden-path sentences: complement-clause (NP/S, easy) and subordinate-clause (NP/Z, hard) ambiguities, reading-time garden-path effect
paradigms.location: Sec 4 (2 datasets x 24 sets of 4 sentences), Tables 1-2

paradigms.name: Plausibility manipulation within garden-path sentences (implausible sub-phrase shortens garden-path effect and slows reading)

D.population: not_reported (first-pass and total reading times from Pickering & Traxler 1998)
D.metric: garden-path effect and reading time in ms; correlation rho with model measures

effects.es_metric: garden-path effect in ms, first-pass reading time, all items
effects.label: HUMAN-LIKE
effects.location: Table 2 p.172 (first-pass; total-pass IF-min 66.17 vs human 185.5 ms gives ratio 0.36, computed here); rho with human reading time 0.595, p=0.00032, Table 1 p.172; surprisal first-pass GPE 0.35 ms

effects.es_metric: change in garden-path effect (ms) for implausible minus plausible, first-pass, computed here from Table 3
effects.label: DIFFERENT
effects.location: Table 3 p.173: model GPE rises with implausible cues (28.66 to 50.28 ms), human falls (50.5 to 28.5 ms); authors state all measures showed the opposite

E.headline: Incompatibility fractions from GPT-2 completions plus a dependency parser track human garden-path reading times and beat surprisal, but fail on plausibility effects.

G.notes: GPT-2 size, decoding settings and human sample are not stated; no code link. Human numbers are group means from Pickering & Traxler, so ratios compare to a single published study. IF measures are tuned by regression on the same reading times (Table 1), so fit is in-sample. Eligibility borderline: model is a component of a metric.
